{{Short description|American mathematician (1923-1995)}}
'''Joseph Leonard Ullman''' (30 January 1923, in [[Buffalo, New York]] – 11 September 1995, in [[Chelsea, Michigan]]) was a mathematician who worked on [[mathematical analysis|classical analysis]] with a focus on [[approximation theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Assche, Walter|title=Death of Joe L. Ullman (Topic #11)|journal=Op-Sf Net|date=Nov 9, 1995|url=http://math.nist.gov/opsf/personal/op2611.html}}</ref>

Ullman received his A.B. from the [[University of Buffalo]] and his graduate studies were interrupted by service in the U.S. Army in World War II. He was injured, received a [[Purple Heart]], and spent the rest of the war as a mathematics instructor. He received a Ph.D. in 1949 from [[Stanford University]] with thesis ''Studies on Faber Polynomials'' under the direction of [[Gábor Szegő]]. Ullman became an instructor at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1949, an assistant professor in 1954, an associate professor in 1962, and a professor in 1966.

He wrote forty-three research papers. During his career at the University of Michigan he supervised eleven doctoral theses.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/joseph-ullman |title=Joseph Ullman {{!}} Faculty History Project – U. of Michigan |access-date=2012-08-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617033554/http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/joseph-ullman |archive-date=2018-06-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Lachance, Michael|author2=Van Assche, Walter|title=In memoriam: Joseph L. Ullman (1923–1995)|journal=J. Approx. Theory|year=2010|volume=162|issue=4|pages=639–645|url=https://www.math.technion.ac.il/hat/people/obits/ullman.pdf|doi=10.1016/j.jat.2009.05.001|doi-access=free}}</ref>
